text:
Sandis Vilmanis was the 157th pick in the 2022 draft, a project out of Lulea's junior program. On Wednesday in Sunrise he had two goals and two assists in 13:30, and he was in the middle of almost everything that mattered in Florida's 5-3 win over Chicago.

He opened the scoring at 4:43 of the first, with Sam Reinhart and Carter Verhaeghe assisting. Verhaeghe made it 2-0 on the power play at 12:29, set up by both Tkachuks, Brady and Matthew. Vilmanis then fed Seth Jones for a 3-0 lead at 13:20 of the second, on a shot that had only a 5% chance of going in.

Chicago did not fold. Roman Kantserov scored at 16:48 of the second, with Connor Bedard on the assist, and Frank Nazar scored shorthanded on a backhand 9:31 into the third to make it 3-2. Vilmanis answered 90 seconds later with an unassisted slap shot that pushed Florida's win chance from 84% to 96%. Nazar refused to go away, scoring again at 16:09 on a 3% chance, the least likely goal of the night, with Bedard picking up his second assist. Reinhart sealed it at 18:33 on a 76% look, assisted by Vilmanis.

Florida deserved it. Expected goals finished 4.06 to 2.23, the Panthers took 60 shot attempts to 45, and replay every shot and they win 68% of the time. Reinhart's own chances were worth 1.60 expected goals on six shots, and he was on the ice for 3.22 expected goals for against 0.54 against. The goaltending was the shaky part on both sides: Jacob Markstrom allowed three on 20 shots, and Spencer Knight allowed 0.7 goals more than expected.

For the Blackhawks, Nazar's two goals and Bedard's two assists were the bright spots in a fourth straight game without a win (0-3-1). Florida also won the first meeting, 3-2 on Oct. 25. Chicago's problem isn't heart; it is that 2.23 expected goals rarely beats a team that creates four.
headline: Vilmanis has the night of his life as Florida holds off Chicago
